Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

depress verb

make someone sad, dishearten

also depressing, depressed, be depressed, lose heart, dishearten, discourage

classical

Cic. Tusc. 4.34: animōs adflīgere et dēbilitāre metū (Lewis & Short)

afflīgō (adflīgō), afflīgere, afflīxī, afflīctum

verb, third conjugation

cast down, dishearten

Literally to dash to the ground; of the spirits, to cast down. Afflīctus is downcast, wretched (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • animum dēmittere — lose heart, be downcast

    also used · classical · Cic. Fin. 5.42; Cic. Tusc. 4.14 (Lewis & Short)

    To let one’s spirits sink: what a person does who is depressed. Its opposite is animōs tollere (Lucilius, in Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • sī vīcerint, efferunt sē laetitiā; victī dēbilitantur animōsque dēmittunt

    if they win, they are carried away with joy; beaten, they lose their strength and their spirits sink (of children at play)Cic. Fin. 5.42 (Lewis & Short)

See also sad, sadness, gloomy, encourage.

SourcesLewis & Short: affligo · Lewis & Short: demitto
